meeting_header:
Date: 2027-01-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Evan Brooks (Redwood CSM), Maria Gonzalez (Newbridge Head of IT), Dr. Alan Shore (CISO), Ben Carter (Platform Eng), Lisa Cho (Compliance)
summary: POC scoping focused on security/compliance requirements for a Newbridge Health pilot. Discussed success criteria, workload sizing and benchmarks, timelines, and specific security controls (SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs). Agreed next steps: Redwood to share compliance docs and benchmark plan; Newbridge to provide workload samples and set up SSO test accounts. Pilot target week of 2027-01-20.
topics: Benchmark plan and metrics (latency, p99, cost/TOK)
Audit logs, retention and access control
transcript: [00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from my side, I'm Jordan AE on Redwood. Priya our SE and Evan CSM here.
[00:18] Maria Gonzalez: Hi all, Maria here. we're looking to run a security-first pilot for an internal docs assistant across several clinics.
[00:30] Dr. Alan Shore: Alan, CISO. primary concerns are PHI handling, audit trails, and certs - SOC2 and ISO are must-haves.
[00:47] Jordan Lee: totally, that's what today's for. Priya can walk through how we handle SOC2/ISO and what we can share for the pilot.

[01:10] Priya Menon: hi. quick overview - for hosted we have SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001 certs, we can share the attestation and scoping. for private deployments we support customer KMS and HSM integration, and VPC peering for network isolation.
[01:35] Ben Carter: do you support on-prem or only VPC? any air-gapped option?

[01:45] Priya Menon: we support Private deployments (VPC and on-prem packages). for pilots most customers start with a VPC/private cloud config to test SSO/SAML and RBAC, then consider on-prem if needed. there is often some setup time for on-prem.
[02:05] Lisa Cho: audit logs: what fields do you capture and retention windows? we need 7 years for certain logs by policy.

[02:18] Priya Menon: we capture request metadata, token usage, model/version, timestamps, caller identity, and redaction flags. retention configurable; default retention is 90 days but enterprise add-on supports longer retention - we can provide options up to multi-year via archiving to customer S3.
[02:40] Dr. Alan Shore: important that logs are immutable and stored with proper encryption and key management. can you integrate with our KMS?
[02:50] Jordan Lee: yes, KMS integration is supported for Private and Dedicated. Hosted customers can also use bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM support on higher-tier plans.
[03:10] Maria Gonzalez: success criteria for pilot - what would we measure?

[03:20] Priya Menon: we typically agree on functional accuracy for a set of eval prompts, latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99), throughput for concurrent sessions, and security checks (SSO success, RBAC enforcement, audit log completeness).
[03:40] Ben Carter: for workload sizing - our anticipated avg per clinic is ~5k requests/day, peak bursts up to 200 qps for short windows. looking for cost estimates and GPU sizing for that.

[03:58] Priya Menon: noted. for 5k/day with peaks at 200 qps we'd recommend a small dedicated pool (1-2 A100 equiv) for predictable latency or hosted with burst capacity. we'll run a quick benchmark to size precisely - i'll propose GPU hours and quantization tradeoffs.
[04:20] Jordan Lee: any regulatory constraints on data residency?
[04:25] Lisa Cho: data must stay in US regions; encryption at rest and in transit and SOC2 cert are required.
[04:35] Priya Menon: we can pin the pilot to a US region and enable customer-managed keys. also can implement prefix caching and token redaction to limit PHI exposure.
[05:00] Ben Carter: benchmarks - what tests do you run? we need p99 latency under 800ms for short-turn queries, and end-to-end throughput for document indexing tasks.

[05:15] Priya Menon: benchmark plan we'll share includes synthetic traffic replay, representative prompt set (we'll ask you for samples), and metrics: latency p50/p95/p99, token/sec, cost per 1k tokens, model output quality vs our baseline. we'll also run failure/fallback tests to validate graceful degradation.
[05:40] Maria Gonzalez: about SSO - we use SAML 2.0 with Azure AD. want to test SSO for two roles: admin and analyst. RBAC enforcement needs to prevent export of PHI by analysts.

[05:58] Priya Menon: we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC; we can set up a test SAML app. RBAC is role-based with custom policies - can restrict model access and data export. we'll ask for a matrix of roles and permissions.
[06:20] Dr. Alan Shore: encryption - keys, rotation, and proof of key custody? also who has access to logs?
[06:30] Jordan Lee: keys can be customer-managed via KMS; rotation policies supported. access to logs is restricted via RBAC; we can export logs to your storage for custody.
[06:45] Ben Carter: what's the timeline to get a pilot up and running?
[06:52] Evan Brooks: typically 2-3 weeks for a security-focused pilot: week 1 setup and SSO, week 2 benchmark run and tuning, week 3 review and handoff. we can compress if all inputs are ready.
[07:10] Maria Gonzalez: sounds good - we are targeting the week of Jan 20 for the benchmark run as you suggested.
[07:18] Priya Menon: action items - we'll send a benchmark plan and a short checklist for SAML and RBAC mapping. please provide sample prompts (redacted) and expected pass/fail criteria for quality.
[07:32] Ben Carter: one more thing - data retention rules for audit logs. we may need to hold certain logs for 7 years. can Redwood archive logs to our S3 with immutability?
[07:45] Priya Menon: yes, archive to customer S3 with bucket lock for immutability is supported for enterprise add-on. we'll include retention options in the compliance pack.
[08:00] Maria Gonzalez: are there any known limitations re: PHI and model caching? we want to avoid leakage across tenants.

[08:12] Priya Menon: we have tenant isolation and prefix/KV cache controls. for PHI heavy workloads we recommend disabling shared prefix caching and using customer-dedicated caches or private deployments.
[08:30] Dr. Alan Shore: good - we will likely want RBAC to block exports and a dedicated cache for our tenant.
[08:40] Jordan Lee: noted. i'll include config recommendations in the pilot doc: dedicated cache, BYOK, VPC peering, and RBAC rules to block export.
[09:00] Ben Carter: about benchmarks - can we test both hosted and dedicated variants to compare latency/cost?
[09:10] Priya Menon: absolutely, we can run both: hosted with burst and dedicated reserved pool. that will help you decide on Dedicated vs Hosted for production.
[09:28] Maria Gonzalez: compliance docs - please send SOC2 Type II report and ISO27001 cert, plus a data processing addendum (DPA).
[09:40] Jordan Lee: we'll send SOC2 and ISO certs and a template DPA. Evan will attach the DPA and our security whitepaper.
[09:55] Lisa Cho: also we need to run a penetration test or vendor security questionnaire. do you support pen testing?

[10:05] Priya Menon: we can provide a pen-test summary and support vendor questionnaires. full penetration testing for private/on-prem deployments can be arranged with a scoped process; for hosted we provide our compliance artifacts and SOC attestations.
[10:22] Ben Carter: for workload sizing - Priya mentioned quantization tradeoffs. any quick guidance on model choice affecting cost?

[10:32] Priya Menon: yes, smaller quantized models reduce cost and latency but may affect quality. we'll include quality vs cost deltas in the benchmark and propose a model family to test (e.g., 7B quant vs 13B quant).
[10:50] Maria Gonzalez: ok next steps recap please

[10:55] Jordan Lee: recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO/DPA, Priya sends benchmark plan and sizing, Ben supplies workload samples and SSO test account details, Lisa confirms retention requirements. target benchmark week of Jan 20. Jordan/Evan to schedule follow-ups.
[11:20] Dr. Alan Shore: thanks, prioritize the audit log immutability and KMS integration in the docs.
[11:28] Evan Brooks: noted. i'll set calendar invites for setup sessions and the benchmark run. expect emails from us tomorrow with attachments.
[11:40] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone. we'll follow up.
[44:00] (call end)
